scope_note: Amazon review logs dominate every split (8 of 10 discovery logs, 12 of 14 holdout logs). A 'confirmed' verdict therefore means 'confirmed on Amazon-dominated logs'; the non-Amazon means are reported separately. Nine of the holdout logs were used in the earlier tracking study (they chose the baseline half-life 2); only the 5 fresh Amazon categories are completely new.

hypotheses.name: batch the questions
hypotheses.statement: Asking every second round (the people of two rounds at once, unspent budget carried forward) instead of every round loses less than 0.01 NDCG.
hypotheses.prediction: Holds. Informed by generation 1: the 'batching is worse' claim (H5) was killed at screen with a mean difference of about 0.0003.

hypotheses.name: how many rows per person
hypotheses.statement: Letting each person report at most 10 rows per round loses less than 0.01 NDCG.
hypotheses.prediction: Holds only where people report few rows; generation 1 showed a cap of 3 loses about 0.05, so 10 may still fail on heavy-user logs.

hypotheses.name: threshold on the running count
hypotheses.statement: Publishing only items whose decayed report count is at least 3 loses less than 0.01 NDCG.
hypotheses.prediction: Holds. Generation 1 showed a per-round threshold of 2 loses 0.06 to 0.10 because most items are reported once per round, but items in the top 100 accumulate counts over rounds.

hypotheses.name: damp heavy hitters
hypotheses.statement: Summing per-round shares raised to the power 0.5 (so a few heavy items cannot crowd out rising ones) gives a better list than plain shares.
hypotheses.prediction: Fails: generation 1 killed every variant that changes the weighting of the baseline.

gates.unit: Everything is judged SEPARATELY for each n (people per round) on the logs eligible at that n; at least min_logs_per_n logs are required, otherwise that n is 'not testable'. A missing expected cell makes the whole stage INCOMPLETE (no verdict).
gates.screen: n = 30 and 100, 6 draws, own draws. Keep a hypothesis if its primary rule moves the right way at any tested n: superiority mean diff > +0.005; noninferiority mean diff > -0.01; dominated mean diff < -0.005.
gates.full: PASS at an n: superiority = mean diff >= +0.01 AND diff>0 in >=70% of logs AND one-sided t lower bound at level alpha/(family*3) > 0; noninferiority = t lower bound of mean diff > -0.01 AND worst log diff > -0.03; dominated = mean diff <= -0.01 AND diff<0 in >=70% of logs AND t upper bound < 0. A hypothesis advances if it PASSES at one or more n.
gates.holdout: same rule at level alpha/3 for each n, plus the mean diff on the fresh logs alone must have the same sign (superiority > 0; noninferiority > -0.01; dominated < 0). CONFIRMED only at the n values that PASS both discovery and holdout.
gates.robust: Confirmed hypotheses are rerun with 60 windows (rounds half as long) at n=100 on all logs and must pass the holdout rule again; a claim that does not hold at 60 windows is reported as confirmed only at 30 windows.

designed_after: Generation 2 was designed after the generation-1 screen and its discovery-log numbers were seen (all six generation-1 rules were killed at screen; no rule was evaluated on any holdout log). The family size counts all 10 hypotheses tried so far, so the multiple-testing level is stricter. Holdout logs are still unopened for every rule.
